core_obligations: Set up the functor (proof lines 23186-23192): work with the 2-fibre product category; the functor sends F to the triple (f^{-1}F, i^{-1}F, c) where c : j^{-1}f^{-1}F -> g^{-1}i^{-1}F is the canonical isomorphism.

Construct the quasi-inverse (proof lines 23193-23215): for an object (F', G, alpha) of the target, proper base change gives i^{-1}f_*F' = g_*j^{-1}F', and g_*alpha turns this into a map to g_*g^{-1}G; from the resulting maps i_*G -> i_*g_*g^{-1}G and f_*F' -> i_*g_*g^{-1}G one sets F = f_*F' x_{i_*g_*g^{-1}G} i_*G.

Compute the stalks (proof lines 23216-23245): if x is not in Z then x comes from a unique geometric point x' of X' and the two factors i_*G and i_*g_*g^{-1}G have singleton stalks, so F_x = F'_{x'}; if x is in Z with a geometric point z over it, the stalk of f_*F' is Gamma(X'_x, F'|X'_x) and that of i_*g_*g^{-1}G is Gamma(E_z, g^{-1}G|E_z), and since E_z = X'_x and alpha identifies the two sheaves there, one gets F_x = G_z.

Finish (proof lines 23246-23254): there are canonical maps i^{-1}F -> G and f^{-1}F -> F' compatible with alpha whose stalk maps are the isomorphisms computed above; the author states that the careful construction of these maps is omitted, which is the routine closing step of the argument.
proof_roadmap: Write the functor on triples using the canonical comparison isomorphism.
Build the quasi-inverse as a fibre product of pushforwards, using proper base change and the gluing isomorphism alpha.
Verify the two round trips by computing stalks at points outside and inside Z, the routine construction of the final canonical maps being the only step the author leaves to the reader.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the gluing statement for etale sheaves along a proper modification that is an isomorphism outside a closed subscheme: the sheaves on X are the fibre product of those on X' and Z over E (statement lines 23166-23183). The proof (proof lines 23185-23254) writes down the functor on triples, constructs the quasi-inverse as the fibre product f_*F' x_{i_*g_*g^{-1}G} i_*G using proper base change and the gluing isomorphism, and verifies both round trips by an explicit stalk computation, split into the cases x not in Z and x in Z with the identification E_z = X'_x. H2: an explicit construction plus a two-case stalk computation.
